prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1208; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end impact while the insured vehicle was parked in a lot, and the claim was opened the same day with a request for a rental.
Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office. Future requests will be routed accordingly.
Entry 4: Responding officer's notes place the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. No witness account, photographs or separate report of the impact have been located.
Entry 5: Inspection of the vehicle shows damage to the rear bumper and tail lamp housing. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspections.
Entry 6: Repair estimate has been received, but it is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage came from this impact or from other causes.
Entry 7: Claimant's initial statement was recorded by phone. A follow-up interview added a few minor details about position and speed, but the core account stayed the same.
Entry 8: Medical records show a neck and back strain, which is a plausible injury for a collision of this type. Claimant was referred for physical therapy.
Entry 9: Prior records show treatment to the same body area within the last two years. That earlier condition appears to add to the current complaints and will be considered in evaluating the injury.
Entry 10: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. Latest therapy notes describe reduced pain and better range of motion.
Entry 11: File reviewed and sent to the bodily injury unit for evaluation. Liability and damage questions remain open pending the repair review and the claimant's counsel's response.
